q: What must an ISO 14064-1 GHG report contain?
title: What goes in an ISO 14064-1 GHG report
short: An ISO 14064-1 report must describe the organisation, period and boundaries, give direct emissions by gas in tonnes CO2e, biogenic CO2 and removals separately, indirect emissions by category, the base year, methods and factors, uncertainty, exclusions, and say whether it was verified. It also names the GWP values used.
audience: Sustainability leads preparing for ISO 14064-3 verification

ul: The reporting organisation and the person responsible for the report.
The organisational boundary and the consolidation approach: control or equity share.
The reporting boundary: which indirect emission categories are included, and the criteria you used to decide which are significant.
Direct (Category 1) emissions in tonnes CO2e, with each gas shown separately: CO2, CH4, N2O, NF3, SF6, and HFC and PFC groups.
Biogenic CO2 from burning biomass, and direct removals, reported separately from the totals.
Indirect emissions by ISO category 2 to 6, for the ones you judged significant.
Any significant sources excluded, with the reason.
The base year, its emissions, and any recalculation with the reason.
The quantification methods, and any change from the last report.
The emission and removal factors used, or a reference to them, and the GWP values with their IPCC source.
The effect of uncertainty on the accuracy of the results.

sections.h: Statements a verifier will look for
p: The report must state that it was prepared in line with ISO 14064-1, and whether it has been verified, with the type of verification and level of assurance. Behind it, a verifier working to ISO 14064-3 will want the records that support each figure: bills, invoices, meter readings and the calculation sheets. Check clause wording against your purchased copy, because the standard also lists recommended items, such as reduction initiatives, that are optional.

example.title: Worked example: Category 1 shown by gas
lines: Diesel: 50,000 litres x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre = 134,000 kg, 134.0 t CO2
R-32 top-ups: 10 kg x 677 (AR5) = 6,770 kg, 6.77 t CO2e as HFCs
Category 1 total: 134.0 + 6.77 = 140.77 t CO2e, reported as 134.0 t CO2 and 6.77 t CO2e HFCs, GWP basis IPCC AR5
